missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1: cycle 1 with a black-standard thermometer (65 ± 3 °C) or cycle 4 with a black-panel thermometer (63 ± 3 °C), exposure periods of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) or 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall not include any logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be permitted to have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
The ESA representative of its type shall have a measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

For pulse 2a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +37 V (12V system) or +37 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V (12V system) or +20 V (24V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V (12V system) or +150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) can only be removed with the use of tool(s) in case of replaceable light source module(s).
The stop lamp shall emit red light.
The measured values shall not deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
The measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12 for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3.

extra.text: The ESA sample(s) of the rear lamp shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.

An ESA brought to the market as a replacement part does not need a type approval only if it is obviously marked as a replacement part by an identification number and if it is identical and from the same manufacturer as the corresponding original equipment.

In case the ESA is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall specify the approval number according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128 granted to this ESA, or provide a test report by a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.

If the ESA is sold as aftermarket equipment intended for installation in motor vehicles and is not related to immunity related functions (see paragraph 2.12.), a declaration shall be issued by the manufacturer that the ESA fulfils the requirements of this Regulation and in particular the limits defined in paragraphs 6.5., 6.6., 6.7., 6.8. and 6.9. of this Regulation.
The representative ESA system(s) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6. and, if applicable, paragraph 7. of this Regulation for type approval to be granted.
In case the ESA is (part of) a light source and the documentation as specified in paragraph 3.2.10. is missing, approval of this ESA according to Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.
The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
The approval mark of the ESA shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The approval mark of the ESA shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.

Before testing, a test plan shall be prepared in conjunction with the manufacturer, which contains at least mode of operation, stimulated function(s), monitored function(s), pass/fail criterion(criteria) and intended emissions.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.

The maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA shall be +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems, as given in Table 1.

For the ALSE method, the ESA shall be tested at 30 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 25 V/m over the whole of the 80 to 2,000 MHz range, and at 10 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 8 V/m over the whole of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range (Tables 2a and 2b).
For the stripline method, the ESA shall be tested in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range at 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a) and a minimum of 50 V/m over the whole band (Table 2b).

For the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall be tested at 21 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 18 V/m over the whole of the LUF to 2,000 MHz range, and at 7 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 6 V/m over the whole of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range (Tables 2a and 2b).
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.

In the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).

In the frequency range 75-400 MHz, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).

In the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the narrowband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.).
For an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω AN as defined in Figure 1 shall be used.
The AN(s) used for testing the LV-powered ESA shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The grounding connection of the AN(s) used for testing the LV-powered ESA shall be bonded to the ground plane.
Measurement ports of AN(s) used for testing the LV-powered ESA shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.

The AN impedance ZPB shall be within a tolerance of ± 20 % of the characteristic shown in Figure 2 in the measurement frequency range of 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz, measured between terminals P and B with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port and terminals A and B short circuited.
The approval mark affixed to the ESA shall follow the layout of Model A or Model B (see paragraph 5.2. of this Regulation), with the characteristic dimension a of at least 6 mm.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with dipped beams ON (manual mode), the lighting (front light and rear light, including the rear position lamps) shall not switch OFF.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the brake pedal not depressed, there shall be no unexpected activation of brake and no unexpected activation of stop lights.

In the "Brake mode" vehicle immunity test, with the brake pedal depressed to activate the brake function and the stop lights without any dynamic cycle, the stop lights shall not be inactivated during the mode.
If not otherwise stated in Annex 7, the measurement of broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
During the radiated broadband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
If the radiated broadband emission test is not performed with a REESS, the ESA should be tested at rated current.

For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the radiated broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
To ensure that there is no extraneous noise or signal of a magnitude sufficient to affect materially the measurement, ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test.

In the ambient measurement, the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
The radiated broadband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
If peak detectors are used for the radiated broadband emission measurement, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.

The radiated broadband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2 (30 to 1,000 MHz: peak RBW 100/120 kHz, min scan time 100 ms/MHz; quasi-peak RBW 120 kHz, min scan time 20 s/MHz; scanning receiver BW 120 kHz, max step 60 kHz, min dwell 5 ms peak / 1 s quasi-peak).

If FFT-based measuring instruments are used, they shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode).
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
The radiated broadband emission test of the ESA shall be performed at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.
Unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.
The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation.

If the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the frequency range may be divided into the 14 frequency bands 30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz, with tests at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band, to confirm that the ESA meets the requirements of Annex 7.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
If not otherwise stated in Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic emissions test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
The narrowband emissions test of the ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.

Where an open area test site (OATS) is used as an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) for the narrowband emissions test of the ESA, the OATS shall comply with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4 (see Figure 1 of the appendix to Annex 7).

Ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main narrowband test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.

The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Tables 1 and 2 (spectrum analyser: 30 to 1,000 MHz, RBW 100/120 kHz at -3 dB, minimum scan time 100 ms/MHz; scanning receiver: 30 to 1,000 MHz, BW 120 kHz at -6 dB, maximum step size 60 kHz, minimum dwell time 5 ms).
Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments used for conformity measurements shall meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1.

In the event that the narrowband limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.

Where the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, and the frequency range is divided into the 14 frequency bands (30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz), tests shall be performed at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band to confirm that the ESA meets the requirements of Annex 8.

The ESA may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that these result in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered: (a) Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) Stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) Reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
The frequency range and general test conditions for the immunity tests of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
The test conditions for the ESA during immunity tests to electromagnetic radiation shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in this Annex unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
Any extraneous equipment required to operate the ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase.
No extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.
To ensure reproducible measurement results, the test signal generating equipment and its layout shall be to the same specification as that used during each appropriate calibration phase.

If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit, the interconnecting cables should ideally be the wiring harnesses as intended for use in the vehicle; if these are not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard.
If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit, all cables in the wiring harness should be terminated as realistically as possible and preferably with real loads and actuators.
The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.

The immunity test of the ESA shall be performed at the intervals specified in ISO 11452-1, throughout the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz, unless a reduced number of spot frequencies is used on the basis of manufacturer data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority.
If an ESA fails the tests defined in this Annex, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
When the absorber chamber test is used, the "substitution method" shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
When the absorber chamber test is used, the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
When TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.
When TEM cell testing is used, the method of maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM-cell shall be chosen depending on the ESA to be tested.

When bulk current injection testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, either with the BCI substitution method and the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or with the BCI closed loop method and the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.

When bulk current injection testing is performed with the ESA installed in the vehicle as an alternative, it shall be performed according to ISO 11451-4 with the BCI substitution method and the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
When the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
Unless otherwise specified, the reverberation chamber testing method shall be carried out using a test setup with ground plane.
The test method shall ensure the immunity of the ESA (rear combination lamp) to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The test method shall limit conducted transients from the ESA (rear combination lamp) to the vehicle power supply.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface).

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical the pair requirements of paragraph 5.5. shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps shall not be reciprocally incorporated.

Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.

Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, based upon the areas bounded by the outline of their light emitting surfaces, shall not overlap.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing those projections, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) (interdependent lamp system) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

For two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip, the illumination of such a surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

For lamps in the shape of a band or strip whose light-emitting surface is constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements, these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and not less than 0.8 m long; the illumination shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends, and juxtaposed light-emitting elements, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
The maximum height above the ground of the lamps shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of the lamps, as regards width, shall be determined from that edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is the furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps.

For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

The electrical connections shall be such that the main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps cannot be switched ON unless the lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11. (including the rear position lamps) are also switched ON, except for main-beam or dipped-beam headlamps used for luminous warnings by intermittent or alternate lighting up at short intervals.
The concealment of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be prohibited.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.

The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
The lamp may be installed on movable components only provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.

Rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.

Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector functions on movable components are obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D", at least one of the lamps shall meet the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable components.

Rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only where additional lamps for these functions are fitted and switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, provided that these additional lamps satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

Where the rear position lamp function is obtained by an interdependent lamp system completely mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1. shall be satisfied, or additional lamps switched ON in any fixed open position shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

Where the rear position lamp function is obtained by an interdependent lamp system partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s); the inwards geometric visibility is deemed satisfied if they still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution.
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When the lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

If the requirement of paragraph 5.21. is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

Where more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface of the lamp in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road, for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road; this does not apply to retro-reflectors (paragraph 5.21.3.).
With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
For lamps approved with replaceable light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement.

In the case where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

A temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed only provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
In case of a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.

During temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

For rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, the intensity of all such lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

For rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

For R2 rear position lamps and S2 stop lamps with variable luminous intensity control, increase and decrease of the luminous intensity in relation to environmental conditions (ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds, contamination of the light emitting surface) shall be within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations.

For R2 rear position lamps and S2 stop lamps with variable luminous intensity control, a decrease of the luminous intensity due to traffic conditions, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, shall only be activated when the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m, and an already activated decrease may remain active only as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h.
Stop lamps of category S4 may produce variable luminous intensity, based on the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., independently from the other lamps.
For lamps with variable luminous intensity, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.

For vehicles of M and N categories, the electric power supply conditions for the devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. shall comply with the provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. and 5.27.2. when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

The provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. and 5.27.2. shall not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
If measurements of geometric visibility are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
A LED module may be non-replaceable only if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.
In case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of the UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle approved according to this Regulation and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.

Lamps equipped with LED substitute light source(s) shall be used only where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive, and the presence of the marking on the lamps related to the use of LED substitute light source(s) shall be checked at type approval and conformity of production.
The reversing lamp shall be present on motor vehicles (mandatory).
On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device is mandatory and a second device is optional.
For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility defined by angle α as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.

For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, if there is only one device, the geometric visibility defined by angle β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be β = 45° to right and to left.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
For the reversing lamp, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be mandatory on all categories of vehicles (including M1).
Stop lamp devices of S3 or S4 category shall be mandatory on M1 category vehicles.

The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of an S3 or S4 category device shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 categories stop lamps.
In length, S1 or S2 categories stop lamps shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
For stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
Where an S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
The stop lamps need not function only if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
Rear position lamps of R or R1 or R2 categories shall be mandatory.
Where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The rear position lamps shall be oriented rearwards.
In all cases, the distance between the rear fog-lamp and each stop-lamp shall be greater than 100 mm.

Where the parking lamp function is performed by the front and rear position lamps according to paragraph 6.12.9., the rear position lamps shall be able to operate even if the device which starts the propulsion system is in a position which makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate, and a device which automatically switches OFF these lamps as a function of time is prohibited.

Where the parking lamp function is performed by simultaneously switching ON the front and rear position lamps on the same side of the vehicle according to paragraph 6.12.9., the connection shall allow the rear position lamp(s) on the same side of the vehicle to be switched ON independently of any other lamps.
If an end-outline marker lamp tell-tale exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.

The position of an end-outline marker lamp in relation to the corresponding rear position lamp shall be such that the distance between the projections on a transverse vertical plane of the points nearest to one another on the apparent surfaces in the direction of the respective reference axes of the two lamps considered is not less than 200 mm.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is mandatory on motor vehicles.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) are permitted only provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
The orientation of the rear retro-reflector shall be rearwards.
The rear retro-reflector, triangular, is prohibited on motor vehicles; the rear retro-reflector of the lamp shall therefore not be triangular.

On M1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON.

The rear position lamps may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON only as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
Conspicuity markings are prohibited on vehicles of category M1; the rear lamp installed on an M1 vehicle shall not incorporate or be supplemented by conspicuity markings.
Where the emergency stop signal is provided by the stop lamps, the emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.

The emergency stop signal shall be present (mandatory) on motor vehicles; where the stop lamps of the rear lamp are used, the emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps fitted.
Where the emergency stop signal is provided by the stop lamps, the number of lamps of the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.2. or 6.7.2.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
If any of the lamps of the emergency stop signal to the rear of the vehicle use filament light sources, the frequency of the emergency stop signal shall be 4.0 +0.0/-1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided or if the hazard warning signal is activated.

If a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer, the control of the emergency stop signal on the motor vehicle shall also be capable of operating the emergency stop signal on the trailer, except as provided in paragraph 6.23.9.2.

When the motor vehicle is electrically connected to a trailer, the operating frequency of the emergency stop signal for the combination shall be limited to the frequency specified in paragraph 6.23.7.1.1., unless the motor vehicle can detect that filament light sources are not being used on the trailer for the emergency stop signal.

If a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer fitted with a service braking system of either continuous or semi-continuous type, it shall be ensured that a constant power supply is provided via the electrical connector for the stop lamps to such trailers while the service brake is applied.

Where the rear position lamps are switched ON as exterior courtesy lamps, the rear position lamps shall not be switched ON as exterior courtesy lamps unless the vehicle is stationary and the propulsion system is stopped, or a driver or passenger door or a load compartment door is opened or after being closed.
Where the rear position lamps are switched ON as exterior courtesy lamps, the rear position lamps operating as exterior courtesy lamps shall be switched OFF when the vehicle is no longer stationary.
Where the rear position lamps are switched ON as exterior courtesy lamps and vary in luminous intensity and/or apparent surface, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.
Where the rear position lamps are switched ON as exterior courtesy lamps, the rear position lamps operating as exterior courtesy lamps shall not flash.

Reversing lamps shall not be switched ON as exterior courtesy lamp(s); approved lamps emitting white light, with the exception of main beam head lamps, daytime running lamps and reversing lamps, and rear position lamps may be switched ON as exterior courtesy lamp(s).

If a lamp function of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the number of lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used, but it may be less than or equal to that number.

If a lamp function of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the arrangement of the lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used.

If a lamp function of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the position in width of the lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used.

If a lamp function of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the geometric visibility of the lamps used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used, although it may be reduced in comparison to those specifications.
If the rear position lamp or reversing lamp of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the answer-back signal shall only operate under the park condition of a vehicle.
If the rear position lamp or reversing lamp of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal and the answer-back signal flashes, the frequency shall not exceed 2.0 Hz.

If a lamp function of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the answer-back signal shall be provided by approved lighting and light-signalling devices where the maximum luminous intensity per lamp does not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line.
The stop lamps of the rear lamp shall not be used to provide the answer-back signal.

If a lamp function of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the answer-back signal may only be activated automatically in conjunction with the locking and unlocking of the door(s) and/or the detection of the vehicle user in proximity to the vehicle.

If a lamp function of the rear lamp is used for the answer-back signal, the duration of the optical indication of the answer-back signal shall not exceed 3 seconds, defined from the beginning to the end of the signal, irrespective of whether it contains flashes, variations of intensity or variations in apparent surface.
If reversing projections are provided on the vehicle, the reversing projections shall be switched ON only when the reversing lamp(s) is/are switched ON.
In the case of reciprocal incorporation where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and "7b" is the apparent surface according to paragraph 2.10.2., F1 shall not be transparent to F2.

For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (paragraph 5.10.4.), the zone 1 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (paragraph 5.10.4.), the zone 1 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in width by a vertical plane which, forming to the front an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, passes through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width.

For the verification of the visibility of a white lamp to the rear (paragraph 5.10.4.), the zone 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground and in width by a vertical plane forming to the rear an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, passing through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width.
If there are several points of contact of the vertical planes delimiting the vehicle's overall width, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.
The values measured for the distances of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

The position of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6., in width, in height and in length shall be checked in accordance with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of this Regulation.

The values measured for the angles of geometric visibility shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The angles of geometric visibility of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7. of this Regulation.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.

The rear position, stop and reversing lamps and their tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
The electrical connections shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the lamps shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the lamps shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.
A separate approval is required for each lamp listed in paragraph 1 (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp).

When two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval may be granted only if each of these lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) satisfy the provisions set out in this Regulation or in another Regulation.
Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of the unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
All the devices of an interdependent lamp system must be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.
The rear position lamp shall be identified by the symbol R1 (steady) or R2 (variable).
The reversing lamp shall be identified by the symbol AR (the letters A and R may be mingled).
The applicable change index for the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall be 0 for the 00 series and 1 for the 01 series of amendments.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
Where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), it shall also bear a marking of the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
Lamps with non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a variable luminous intensity control shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a secondary operating mode shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the approval marking shall be visible after their installation.

Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply, the requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the M1 vehicle category being applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
Where the rear position lamp or stop lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D", it shall be type approved accordingly.

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, a note shall be made within the communication document on whether the functions are provided by multiple light sources or intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single reversing lamp containing more than one light source, the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure shall be produced.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case a light source category or categories or type(s) is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, the applicant for type approval of the lamp shall declare that the lamp is only intended for installation on those vehicles, and this shall be noted in the communication form.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, applying the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed and, where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to that category.
All photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with respect to the conditions of paragraph 4.8., with the particulars of the methods of measurement given in Annex 3.
In the case of replaceable UN approved light sources, all measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.

For replaceable UN approved light source(s) controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the standard light source(s) shall have a luminous flux value that does not deviate more than 5 per cent from its reference/objective luminous flux value when test voltage is applied.

For a lamp (function) using light sources which are subject to more than one of the conditions prescribed in paragraph 4.8., the photometric measurements shall be made separately in accordance with each applicable condition set forth in paragraph 4.8.
For a lamp (function) using light sources subject to more than one condition of paragraph 4.8., all separate measurement results shall be added together.
During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of different positions, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
Where the lamp is also to be approved with LED substitute light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be repeated using the LED substitute light source(s) prescribed.

For a lamp intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, a sample plate or sample plates as supplied shall be positioned in front of the lamp to be tested, in the geometrical position(s) as described in the application drawing(s).
If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
In case the results of measurements are challenged, the distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.

In case the results of measurements are challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver viewed from the reference centre of the light is comprised between 10' and 1 degree.

In case the results of measurements are challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of each light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
For a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.

For a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.

For a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control with replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated at the reference/objective luminous flux or alternatively at a different luminous flux with a proportional correction on the measured luminous intensities.

For lamps equipped with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources, the light sources shall be operated at a voltage or electrical current setting such that the actual luminous fluxes of the light sources do not deviate by more than 5 per cent from the average luminous flux of the light sources.

For lamps equipped with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources, the measured luminous intensities shall be corrected proportionally for the difference between the average luminous flux and the applicable reference/objective luminous flux.

If the applicant requests the additional test to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No. 48, the maximum intensity of the lamp in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall not be more than 2.5∙10-1 cd.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for maximum intensity if all lamps together are lit.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for minimum intensity if either lamp has failed.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

If the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility colorimetric and photometric requirement at all fixed positions of the movable component(s); the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied if these lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.

For systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp under night-time conditions.

For other variable intensity systems, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens).

If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities measured of the two lamps turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by ±5° V and ±10° H of the light distribution table.

If one or both of the reciprocally incorporated rear position and stop lamps contain more than one light source and are considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered for the 5:1 ratio are those obtained with all sources in operation.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
To check the colorimetric characteristics, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of rear position lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 4.

For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4 cd and the maximum luminous intensity shall be 17 cd when used as a single lamp, with the standard light distribution per Figure A3-I.

For rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4 cd and the maximum luminous intensity shall be 42 cd when used as a single lamp (21 cd for a lamp marked "D"), with the standard light distribution per Figure A3-I.
For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady) used as a lamp marked "D", the maximum luminous intensity shall be 8.5 cd.

The rear position lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.

Where the type approval of the reversing lamp is granted with photometric intensity verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards (reversing lamp intended to be installed exclusively in a pair of devices), the device shall only be installed in a pair.

From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the conformity requirements for the lamp shall be considered satisfied if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

With respect to photometric performances, the conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested when testing photometric performances of any lamp chosen at random according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation.

In the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, if the results of the photometric test do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by the production lamps shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.

In the case of non-replaceable filament light source(s) or light source module(s) equipped with non-replaceable filament light source, at any conformity of production check the holder of the type approval shall demonstrate the use in normal production and show the identification of the non-replaceable filament light source(s) as indicated in the type approval documentation.
Tests of conformity of the lamp under this Regulation shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Conformity tests on the lamp shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
The sampled lamp shall be subjected to photometric measurements for the minimum values at the points listed in Annex 3 and the required chromaticity coordinates.

With respect to photometric performance, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any mass-produced lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced lamps shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
The deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four mass-produced lamps selected at random) shall not be more than 20 per cent for the conformity of mass-produced lamps not to be contested.
The approval marking arrangement of the rear combination lamp shall be made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of this Regulation; the arrangements in Annex 7 are examples only.

For the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector in the same assembly, the approval marking shall indicate each function (e.g. R/R2, S/S2, AR, class IA/IB retro-reflector) with the 148R and 150R references and series of amendments, as shown in marking examples 3-a/3-b.
