For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time, if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.

In case a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) are tested and checked for compliance at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

In case a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) are tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1. to 2.1.3. for the combination of them and checked for compliance.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of the lamp (function) are tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
A separate approval is required for the retro-reflector (Class IA or IB) as a retro-reflective device listed in paragraph 1.
The approval number assigned to the approved type of retro-reflector shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.

If the approval granted for the retro-reflector is extended to other such devices differing only in colour, the two samples in any other colour submitted in conformity with paragraph 3.1.1.1. (d) shall be required to meet only the colorimetric and photometric specifications.

The symbol identifying the retro-reflector shall be "IA" for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent) or "IB" for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight, with a minimum "a" of 5 mm, as given in Table 1.

The applicable change index for the retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent, Class IA) or combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight (Class IB) shall be 0 for the 00 series and 1 for the 01 series of amendments, as given in Table 2.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be as defined in Table 1 (minimum 5 mm for Class IA and IB retro-reflectors).
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, the retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.

Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, this marking shall be visible after their installation.

Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
Every modification of the type of retro-reflector shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority which approved the type.

The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in those sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflector; the requirements pertinent to the retro-reflector and to the vehicle category (M1) on which it is intended to be installed shall be applied where their verification at the moment of type approval is feasible.
Ten samples of the retro-reflector shall be submitted for approval and shall be tested in the chronological order as indicated in paragraph 5.1.7.

After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples of the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and at least one hour after this test examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or if necessary in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values after the heat resistance test shall be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.

The first group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

The second group of two retro-reflector samples shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The third group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The fourth group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
One or more or a range of axis of reference, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of coefficients of luminous intensity RI, shall be specified for the retro-reflector.

Where more than one or a range of different axis of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements of the retro-reflector shall be repeated making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified.
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.

For a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, at an angle of divergence of 20', the RI shall be at least 300 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; 200 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; and 100 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.

Where the retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The testing of the colour of the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
The retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB shall be subjected to the tests in the chronological order given in Table 4 (Chronological order of tests, Classes IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB).
For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C), followed by a visual inspection for distortion.
For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall pass a visual inspection of the general specifications and a visual inspection of shapes and dimensions according to Annex 5.

For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the colorimetry shall be checked by visual inspection, with trichromatic coordinates measured in case of doubt, and the photometry shall be checked at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, with complete photometry on the designated samples according to Part 1 of Annex 4.

For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the water test of Part 3 of Annex 6 (10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position) with visual inspection, followed by colorimetry and photometry checks limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the motor fuels test of Part 1 of Annex 7 (5 min) with visual inspection.

For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the oils test of Part 2 of Annex 7 (5 min) with visual inspection, followed by colorimetry and photometry checks limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 hours, a 2 hours interval, 24 hours) with visual inspection.

For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the rear face test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (1 min) with visual inspection, followed by colorimetry and photometry checks limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the stability in time test of Part 3 of Annex 4, followed by colorimetry (visual inspection or trichromatic coordinates) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6, followed by colorimetry (visual inspection or trichromatic coordinates) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the differences of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.

The mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be considered as satisfying the conformity requirements from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

With respect to photometric performance, when testing any mass-produced retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
For mass-produced retro-reflective devices, the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with.

In the first sampling of four retro-reflective devices selected at random (samples A and B), the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B shall not be more than 20 per cent for the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices not to be contested.

One of the retro-reflectors of sample A, after the sampling procedure in paragraph 2., shall be tested for resistance to water penetration according to the procedure described in paragraph 1. of Part 2 of Annex 6. If it fails, both retro-reflective devices of sample B shall pass the same test.
When the RI of the retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device.
If any mirror effect is produced, a reading of the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

For retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP", when the RI is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to this value of ε (minimum RI), and if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference only within ±5° from that position.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°.
If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
The CIE-angular system as shown in Figure A4-I shall be used for specifying and measuring the retro-reflective device.

For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.

For the measurement of the retro-reflective device, the measuring geometry of Figure A4-III shall respect the limits: angular diameter of the source δ ≤ 10', angular diameter of the measuring device γ ≤ 10', angular diameter of the illuminated area η ≤ 80'.
The measuring distance shall be chosen in such an order that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η given in Figure A4-III are respected, but not lower than 10 m.
The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform, with a variation complying with max/min ≤ 1.05.
The photometer head shall be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency for the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.

The photometer head shall not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture; otherwise suitable provisions shall be added, e.g. the application of a diffusing window at a certain distance in front of the sensitive surface.
During photometry of the retro-reflective device, the field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.

During photometry of the retro-reflective device, reflections from the floor and walls which occur over the relatively long test distances used shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.
The residual stray light measured with the sample covered shall be subtracted from the value measured on the retro-reflective device.
Compliance of the retro-reflective device with the shape and dimension specifications shall be verified by visual inspection.

For moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA and IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.

For the water penetration test, the retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.

The water immersion test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The retro-reflective device sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.

If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water on the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit after the water penetration test, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.

If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied to the Class IB retro-reflective device.

The water spray cabinet shall be equipped with a nozzle(s) which provides a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device, with the centreline of the nozzle(s) directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of the rotating test platform.
The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min as measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform.

In the water spray test, a sample device mounted on a test fixture, with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to a water spray according to paragraphs 2.2.1 to 2.2.6 of Annex 6 Part 3.
During the water spray test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
During the water spray test, drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
During the water spray test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

Since the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray test according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.
Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed in the device, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
Upon completion of the drain period, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation.
The test dust used in the dust exposure test shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
In the dust exposure test, a sample device, mounted on a test fixture, with the initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust according to paragraphs 2.3.5 to 2.3.7 of Annex 6 Part 3.
During the dust exposure test, drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.

During the dust exposure test, the test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, and the dust shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.
The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall, and devices with a length exceeding 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.
During the dust exposure test, devices with a length exceeding 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.
During the dust exposure test, the dust shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.

Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection after the corrosion test, the surface shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.
For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB with an accessible mirror-backed rear face, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

After having brushed the rear face, in the case of moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, after which the cloth is removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
For mirror-backed retro-reflective devices with accessible rear face, as soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side shall be brushed with the same brush as before.

For mirror-backed retro-reflective devices with accessible rear face, the RI shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.

The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013, shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity and shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system of the accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be capable to spray a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water used in the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be in accordance to the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The test method used for the accelerated artificial weathering (TM1 Black-standard or TM2 Black-panel thermometer) shall be specified in the report.
In case of retro-reflective devices, the samples shall be exposed to accelerated artificial weathering in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 for a period of 500 hours.

When test method TM1 (Black-standard thermometer) is used, the accelerated artificial weathering shall use cycle No. 1 according to EN ISO 4892-2:2013: 102 min dry / 18 min water spray, broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband (340 nm) irradiance 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², black-standard temperature 65 ± 3 °C and relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.
Preparation of test specimens for the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
For the resistance to fuels test, a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied to the retro-reflective device.

After about five minutes following the wiping with the test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

The outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol.
After the resistance to fuels test, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after the lubricating oil exposure and cleaning, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.
For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after about 5 minutes of exposure to the detergent lubricating oil, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.
In the approval mark affixed to the retro-reflective device, the approval number must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
In the approval mark affixed to the retro-reflective device, the digits constituting the approval number must face the same way as the "E".
In the approval mark affixed to the retro-reflective device, the group of symbols indicating the class must be diametrically opposite the approval number.
